title: Sustainable synthesis of a Co-MOF–ZrO 2  composite for corrosion protection of mild steel in an aggressive acidic environment
content: The development of a highly effective novel corrosion inhibitor for mild steel in severe corrosive environments remains a significant challenge. Herein, we report the synthesis of a Co-HOBt–ZrO2composite through a solvothermal method, involving the incorporation of ZrO2 nanoparticles into a Co-HOBt framework, and its application as a corrosion inhibitor for mild steel. The Co-HOBt–ZrO2 composite material was characterized by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). To evaluate the corrosion inhibition performance of the Co-MOF–ZrO2 composite on mild steel, corrosion studies were conducted in a highly aggressive acidic medium using the gravimetric (mass-loss) method and electrochemical techniques, including electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), potentiodynamic polarization (PDP), and Bode plot analysis. Inclusion of ZrO2 nanoparticles further enhances the MOF's stability and increases its resistive behaviour. Electrochemical results reveal that the Co-MOF–ZrO2 nanocomposite exhibits superior corrosion protection owing to the formation of a strong barrier between mild steel and the aggressive environments. The maximum corrosion inhibition efficiency of 95% was achieved at a concentration of 400 ppm, as determined by potentiodynamic polarization (PDP) measurements. The changes in both anodic (βa) and cathodic (βc) Tafel slopes indicate that the Co-MOF–ZrO2 composite acts as a mixed-type corrosion inhibitor. This study demonstrates the potential of Co-MOF–ZrO2 nanocomposites as an effective corrosion inhibitor for industrial applications such as cleaning industrial machinery parts like acid pickling, descaling, etc.
